ownership: All queries and source passages were authored for JoySearch. Products, facts, values, policies, and organizations are fictional. example.com URLs identify supplied evidence and are never fetched.
purpose: Fresh, predeclared confirmation of ambiguity, navigation, and material-context behavior, with negative controls against over-clarification. Distinct from old fixtures, search relevance, and real-world accuracy.

cases.query: How long can I keep an Atlas session open?

sources.title: Atlas terminal sessions
sources.excerpt: The fictional Atlas terminal service closes an interactive terminal session after six hours. It is unrelated to the Atlas whiteboard product.

sources.title: Atlas whiteboard sessions
sources.excerpt: The fictional Atlas whiteboard product closes a guest collaboration session after forty-five minutes. It is unrelated to the Atlas terminal service.

facets.description: Ask whether the user means the Atlas terminal service or Atlas whiteboard before supplying a session duration.

forbiddenClaims: The user definitely means the terminal service.
The user definitely means the whiteboard product.
Both products have one shared session duration.

cases.query: How do I rotate my key in Kestrel?

sources.title: Kestrel API credential rotation
sources.excerpt: The fictional Kestrel application lets a user rotate a personal API key from Account Settings, then revoke the old API key after updating integrations.

sources.title: Kestrel workspace encryption rotation
sources.excerpt: The fictional Kestrel application uses a separate workspace encryption key. Only a workspace administrator can rotate that key through the Encryption panel. API key rotation does not rotate this key.

facets.description: Ask whether the user means the personal API key or workspace encryption key before choosing a rotation procedure.

forbiddenClaims: Account Settings rotates every kind of key.
Any user can rotate a workspace encryption key.
The user has already specified which key type to rotate.

cases.query: Does the fictional Elm Vault retain deleted items for the same time on every plan? Explain the Trial exception.

sources.title: Elm Vault deletion policy
sources.excerpt: Elm Vault retains deleted items for 21 days on its Standard and Group plans. Its Trial plan is an exception: deleted items are retained for only five days. After the applicable retention period, the items cannot be restored.

facets.description: State that Standard and Group retain deleted items for 21 days.
Explain that Trial instead retains deleted items for five days, so the period is not the same on every plan.

forbiddenClaims: Every plan retains deleted items for 21 days.
Trial retains deleted items for 21 days.
Items remain restorable indefinitely after retention ends.

cases.query: When transferring a fictional Wren document to a new workspace, which export format can be imported, and are comments and attachments preserved?

sources.title: Wren document transfer
sources.excerpt: The fictional Wren editor exports documents as .wren bundles or plain-text .txt files. Only .wren bundles can be imported into another Wren workspace. A .wren import preserves document text and attachments. Comments are excluded from the bundle and are not restored.

facets.description: Specify that .wren bundles can be imported; plain-text .txt exports cannot be imported through this transfer flow.
State that comments are excluded and not preserved by transfer.
State that attachments are preserved by importing the .wren bundle.

forbiddenClaims: Plain-text .txt exports can be imported into Wren workspaces.
Comments are preserved by a .wren import.
Attachments are lost during a .wren import.
